questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Vancouver in Canada due to the nature here. I wanted to go somewhere where i knew i could go on plenty of adventures and experience new things. But going to UBC also made it possible to go to a good school with exciting courses, which definitely was a motivation for going here too. Furthermore Canada is an english speaking country which made it easy to integrate with the culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to figure out how the whole applying for courses worked and how you could change them, but i figured out that you can do that as well when you arrive. Otherwise it was easy to find information and you had people at go global you could write to if doubt of anything. We didn't have a lot of preparation from University of Copenhagen i would say, so some things you have to figure out yourself, and be sure to keep track of all deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I feel like i got the help i needed. There is a go global office you can go to if you have any questions, but also you talk to people who knows how everything works. So i didn't find it very difficult once i got here. Sometimes the mails they sent out could be a little confusing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: No, there is definitely a lot of competition for housing and it can be quite expensive. For sure everything will work out - many people i know traveled to Canada without housing and found it when they got here as it can be difficult to do online. But it is expensive and a bit stressful!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You should know that living in Vancouver is quite expensive and that you might live far away from campus. But you might also get the chance to live somewhere cool in Vancouver and maybe experience the city more. People that live ON campus often stay there a lot. Even though you have the intention of going to the city it just doesn't happen that much if you live on campus. So embrace the off-campus experience!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I recommend applying for on campus housing as it's cheaper and less stressful. But don't be sad if you don't get it - living off-campus can be very good as well and you won't be isolated from other people just because you don't live on campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult to registrate at UBC, because they want you to make a list of 10 courses that doesn't overlap which is impossible and without any restricted courses. Let me just tell you now that it's impossible. Do your best, and it will be fine. Don't use too much time on in.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to make a list of 10 courses in prioritized from 1-10.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not that much - you have to do most yourself. Even if you want other courses, but if you don't get the courses you want you can change it when you get there.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first i didn't get exactly what i wanted. But i changed 2 out of 3 when i got here to courses i would rather have and it turned out great.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out different courses in the beginning of the semester and see what you like. Professors are everything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The BA courses here goes from 100-400. I had two 300 level courses and one 200 level courses. The level really depends on whether you've had the material before. You would normally go for 300 and 400 courses in your third year of BA, but if you would like to try something new, go after 100-200 courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only had lectures with a lot of people, and in contrast to Denmark no one knows each other in the classes. Everyone is new, so don't be scared to reach out. You can also have smaller classes called tutorials or lab classes. Depends on the courses you take.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
200 Cognitive Systems (COGS)
306 Principles of Animal Behavior (PSYC)
301 Brain Dysfunction and Recovery (PSYC)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved 306 Principles of Animal behavior because it's very different and the teacher is great. 301 was also good, a beginner courses for neuroscience. I didn't like Cognitive Systems that much - too abstract for my taste.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Expect to use more money than you thought you would. Everything cost money. And you don't want to miss out on experiences which also cost some money, but are definitely all worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is expensive (vegetables at least). 
Housing more expensive (i gave 6000kr per month but expect to give more if you live off campus)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UBC has A LOT of clubs you can join. If you have an interest there's is 99% a club for it at UBC. So plenty of opportunity to sign up for clubs (anything from sports to knitting to equestrian).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend going out in the nature and hike hike hike! So many beautiful trips you can take over here. Also join clubs if you want friends other that danish people and other exchange students!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hike:) Go to banff and Jasper. And don't be afraid to skip a couple of days of school.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Canadian people are very nice and it's not that different a culture from Denmark. So it came very naturally to me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in class! Everybody is eager to talk to people in the beginning of the semester because no one knows each other in the classes. And it's not weird to say hello to random people over here, it's just us Danish people that are a bit reserved.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of the Canadians

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Buy a student skipass if you want to go ski
Definitely invest your time on adventures not on school - you will for sure pass your exams.
Don't be scared to join new things, it's never as scary as you think

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Brings nips if you want your room to feel homey and cozy

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned to be more independent and proactive. Learning that school isn't everything and you should go out more and take initiative to do stuff. And i would never have been without all my experiences i got over here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can fell lonely sometimes, but it will pass.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
